Mostly fine, just a few nits

Nit, bitwise constants like this were the bain of my existence when I was learning pldm. I know what this means now when reading it, but something like component comparisonEnforced would be nice... It probably has a real name

There is `include/libpldm/firmware_update.h` which as a bunch of enums with bit positions. Among them also

```
  enum pldm_comp_activation_methods {
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_AUTOMATIC = 0, 
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_SELF_CONTAINED = 1, 
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_MEDIUM_SPECIFIC_RESET = 2, 
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_SYSTEM_REBOOT = 3, 
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_DC_POWER_CYCLE = 4, 
         PLDM_ACTIVATION_AC_POWER_CYCLE = 5, 
         PLDM_SUPPORTS_ACTIVATE_PENDING_IMAGE = 6, 
         PLDM_SUPPORTS_ACTIVATE_PENDING_IMAGE_SET = 7
  };
```

but that is for component activation. Overall i could not find any define for the bit position and in the PDF this bit in `DownstreamDeviceUpdateOptionFlags` also does not have any defined name.

Maybe it did not get defined anywhere because there is only one out of 32 bits being used for anything.

Defined bit mask `PLDM_DD_SELF_CONTAINED_ACTIVATION` as a local const 👍
Why does downstream device record descriptors take a callable??

You are right, this is garbage and copy-pasted code..

Changed it now and defined
```
std::map<uint16_t, std::unique_ptr<pldm::fw_update::DescriptorData>>
pldm::fw_update::DescriptorData::copyDescriptorMap
(const std::map<uint16_t, std::unique_ptr<pldm::fw_update::DescriptorData>>& recordDescriptors)
```

That function can then be used in 4 places to copy the map.

Thanks for finding it 🙏
Nit: can we just collapse all of these #if invocations?

I believe Andrew commented somewhere that he wanted all the tests to be guarded individually. I cannot find it anymore, maybe i am hallucinating..

Anyways, the other tests do that as well, `tests/unit/dsp/firmware_update.cpp` for example, so by doing it like this we are staying on the safe side.

Long-term most of these guards will probably fall off as different functions are stabilized due to usage in other projects. I am not even sure if we need all of these functions to be guarded here.
ok, no worries.

In the v1.3.0 patch you call `pkg.reserve(...)`. Why is this case different?

I used `append_range` there which caused a CI run to fail

https://jenkins.openbmc.org/job/ci-repository/140030/console
```
char; _Alloc = std::allocator<unsigned char>]’ at /usr/include/c++/15/bits/stl_vector.h:1690:27,
    inlined from ‘std::vector<unsigned char> pldm::fw_update::makePkgV1_3_0()’ at ../tests/unit/bindings/cpp/firmware-update-test-v1-3-0.cpp:172:21:
/usr/include/c++/15/bits/stl_uninitialized.h:273:31: error: ‘void* __builtin_memcpy(void*, const void*, long unsigned int)’ offset [50, 108] is out of the bounds [0, 50] [-Werror=array-bounds=]
  273 |               __builtin_memcpy(std::__niter_base(__result),
      |               ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
  274 |                                std::__niter_base(__first),
      |                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
  275 |                                __n * sizeof(_ValT));
      |                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
```

since the failure was related to out-of-bounds access, reserving the capacity fixed it. Since it was part of a test code path i did not investigate further, i only needed the package and `append_range` is a more compact way to write it.

But since we won't be using that function anyways, i don't think it would make much of a difference to reserve capacity given the small size of the package here.

It would just be another constant needing adjustment if someone decides to make changes to the package contents.
Also remove the blank line here and throughout before the `#endif`.
